gaps.sentence: If you ___ a red light, you must stop.
gaps.explanation: General rules use the present simple in the if-clause: come to.

gaps.sentence: Had I realized the danger, I ___ the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Had I realized …' = 'If I had realized …' + would have cancelled.

gaps.sentence: If the hotel ___ a pool, we would book it for the whole team.
gaps.hint: unreal present lack of a facility
gaps.explanation: The hotel does not have a pool now, so the if-clause takes the past simple: had.

gaps.sentence: Should you ___ any problems, please contact support.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you plus infinitive' is a formal way to say 'If you ...': experience.

gaps.sentence: If she ___ here now, she would know exactly what to do.
gaps.hint: unreal present needs the subjunctive were
gaps.explanation: For unreal present conditions, formal English uses 'were' for all persons: were.

gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.

gaps.sentence: If the appeals court ___ the verdict, the case will be reheard in the autumn.
gaps.explanation: Present simple after 'if', will + infinitive in the main clause.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.
